answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, so spawning thousands of sock puppets means locking thousands of deposits. Like a walnut cracking only under real pressure, the bond is slashed when an identity misbehaves, while honest agents earn it back with interest. Reputation then grows like a meadow, slowly, from verifiable work, and no newcomer can leap straight onto the ledge of trusted status without paying that cost first.
